transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM); Sarah Gomez (Pioneer Markets - Head of ML), Raj Patel (Eng Manager), Tina Lee (Security), Owen Park (Platform)

Summary: quick QBR + health check. look at usage/costs, recent p99 latency spike in april, roadmap ask for private deployment pilot, security questions from Tina.

Topics: usage trends, cost optimization, reliability incidents, dedicated vs hosted, private deployment timeline, SOC2/KMS questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining the QBR and health check for Pioneer Markets. want to run through last quarter's usage, costs, and then get into reliability and roadmap.
[00:22] Sarah: thanks, Maya. big picture, things are going well but we saw a cost bump in April when we ramped up nightly summarization jobs. wondering if there's low-hanging ops to reduce spend.
[00:35] Lucas: totally, we looked at your tokens per call and the batching could help. also prefix caching is off for some flows, so KV cache could save a fair amount - though i keep saying KV cache, the transcript sometimes shows K-V cahc, ha.
[00:52] Raj: can you remind us the difference between Dedicated and Hosted? we heard Dedicated gives predictable throughput but is heavier to manage?
[01:06] Maya: yeah good q - hosted is our multi-tenant API with usage billing, fastest to get going. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with commit so you get predictable tails and latency SLOs; less variance for p99 but you pay for reserved capacity.
[01:26] Sarah: last month we had a few p99 spikes ~1.2s to 2.5s on generation endpoints, any insight?
[01:38] Lucas: i pulled the traces - the spikes align with long-context customer queries and occasional cache misses. also saw a few requests routed to a lower-capacity variant during autoscale. we're thinking of adjusting queue weights and enabling prefix caching for the nightly job.
[02:05] Owen: are there any model variants you'd recommend to reduce cost but keep quality? we tried a 13b quantized but saw regressions.
[02:16] Lucas: for summarization, a 7b quantized variant with Redwood Optimize rules (slightly higher temp + beam adjustments) tends to keep acceptable quality and cuts token time ~30%. but we should run evals on your prompt set.
[02:38] Tina: from security side, we need to confirm data residency and key management. does Dedicated support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:50] Maya: yes Dedicated and Private both support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; Private gives you full control for on-prem. we'll share the security deck and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:05] Tina: cool - can you also confirm audit log retention options? compliance requires 7 years for certain logs.
[03:14] Aisha: we'll follow up with the retention matrix. quick note, the audit export currently has a 90-day default but we can propose an enterprise retention addon.
[03:25] Sarah: timeline - if we decide on a private pilot, how long to spin up? we have an internal deadline end of Q3.
[03:33] Maya: typical Private pilot is 4-6 weeks for a minimal deployment, faster if you accept a VPC-hosted private control plane. full on-prem takes longer.
[03:45] Raj: what's the cost delta we'd expect moving from Hosted to Dedicated vs Private? need ballpark to discuss with finance.
[03:53] Maya: high-level: Hosted = pure usage (per-token) with variance; Dedicated = commit + lower per-token cost and predictable infra; Private = platform fee + infra ops. i'll send modeled scenarios for your MTD usage and forecast out 3 months.
[04:10] Lucas: on reliability, we recommend setting up canary routes and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant for non-critical flows to prevent total outage. that will also reduce cost in many cases.
[04:25] Sarah: any documented cases where fallback affected quality badly? we worry about user-facing summary accuracy.
[04:33] Lucas: that's why we suggest A/B testing in Redwood Console first and set thresholds for auto-rollbacks. we've seen good success with canary at 10% traffic.
[04:48] Tina: SAML/SSO - we need to vet SCIM and RBAC. does Redwood support SCIM provisioning?
[04:56] Maya: yes SCIM + SAML supported; we'll share the SSO integration guide.
[05:05] Aisha: action item recap coming at the end; i'll capture owners.
[05:12] Sarah: one more on costs - those nightly jobs are the biggest spike. could we move summarization to a batch window and use a cheaper model variant?
[05:23] Lucas: absolutely. move to off-peak, enable batching, and use prefix caching for repeated prefixes. we can run a job-level config that throttles concurrency to hit cost targets.
[05:40] Raj: on reliability incidents - can you walk through the April incident quickly?
[05:46] Lucas: sure. on April 12th we had a regional capacity pressure which triggered autoscale to route a subset of requests to a lower-capacity tier for ~12 minutes; that caused p99 degradations. long term we recommend dedicated pool for mission-critical endpoints or set routing policies to prefer regions.
[06:10] Sarah: are there any specific logs or dashboards you recommend we watch daily?
[06:15] Aisha: Console -> per-route latency + token cost is highest value; add alert on 95/99 percentile and cost per route. we can provision role-level dashboards for your SREs.
[06:30] Owen: regarding the private pilot, what infra do you need from our side? VPC peering? on-prem we would probably start with VPC and managed control plane.
[06:40] Maya: VPC peering, restricted egress rules, and KMS access if you want CMK. we'll send a checklist.
[06:48] Tina: one compliance detail - does Redwood provide signed attestations for log integrity?
[06:54] Lucas: yes we can provide log hashing and attestations as part of enterprise package; will include in security follow-up.
[07:05] Sarah: ok let's talk usage numbers quickly - April usage was 6.2M tokens (generation) and embeddings 120k. May is trending up.
[07:18] Maya: thanks - i'll put together a breakdown by route to show where tokens are burning. any particular route you want prioritized?
[07:24] Raj: start with the nightly summarization and the customer support triage route.
[07:30] Lucas: noted. we'll also run evals on the summarization prompts to see model quality impact when shifting to 7b.
[07:40] Aisha: quick plugs - onboarding for Dedicated includes a migration checklist and runbook. we can pair on a pilot plan.
[07:50] Tina: can we get an NDA addendum for data residency?
[07:54] Maya: yes we'll coordinate with legal.
[08:00] Maya: ok, recapping next steps - i'll send usage + cost scenarios; Lucas runs latency benchmark and evals; Tina shares compliance requirements; Aisha will draft pilot proposal. we'll target follow-up week of May 18.
[08:15] Sarah: thanks everyone, appreciate the detailed help.
[08:19] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing.

Notes: transcript contains a few mis-transcriptions and informal shorthand (e.g., KV cache noted as KH cache in some exports). References to Redwood products: Redwood Console, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Optimize. Shared artifacts referenced: "Pioneer QBR deck (link)", "usage spreadsheet (link)", "security checklist (link)".
